recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. If Pharmacy wants more detailed MedicationStatement.adherence definitions, handle that as a follow-up in the MedicationStatement adherence issue family rather than as a delayed FHIR-20481 application.
issue_request: FHIR-20481 was a Published/Persuasive Pharmacy issue asking how to represent on-hold MedicationRequest/MedicationStatement medications that might later be stopped. The resolution said a medication should stay on hold unless someone with authority can discontinue it, and approved wording that the prescription may or may not be resumed.
initial_application: Jira records application to build in merge commit 16680e7ffc2f0f3b8cf031ce23e828ec14c2457e. The underlying Pharmacy commit 92cc8632039c231c346b3ab90697c9c0537a1a5f changed the MedicationRequest on-hold definition from expected continuation to might-or-might-not resume; no FHIR-20481-specific MedicationStatement status definition change was found in that patch.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists MedicationRequest and MedicationStatement as active resources. Later Pharmacy decisions FHIR-19468/FHIR-19470, FHIR-32060, FHIR-39271, and FHIR-39333 changed MedicationStatement so status is recorded/entered-in-error/draft and taking/not-taking assertions, including on-hold and stopped, are represented through MedicationStatement.adherence. The combined branch already contains reconciliation commits for FHIR-19470 and FHIR-39271.
reconciliation: No source change was made. MedicationRequest already says the request might or might not be resumed. MedicationStatement no longer has an on-hold status code carrying the old expected-to-resume language; the current adherence model covers on-hold as not-taking without requiring resumption.

related_jiras.note: Introduced MedicationStatement.adherence for taking/not-taking semantics, replacing prior status-based representation for those assertions.
Confirms MedicationStatement.status reflects recording status while MedicationStatement.adherence carries taking/not-taking information; already represented on the combined branch.
Added on-hold and stopped descendants under the MedicationStatement adherence not-taking code.
